title: Performance of GFR Estimation in Finnish Children and Adolescents

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Performance of GFR Estimation in Finnish Children and Adolescents》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · abstract-1-1】The accuracy of estimating glomerular filtration rate (GFR) using endogenous biomarkers has been widely studied, and many GFR estimating equations have been proposed. In this study, we compared the performance of these equations in a Finnish population and evaluated their accuracy in different age groups and categories based on measured GFR (mGFR).

【Body · p0025】The aim of this study was to evaluate the performance of GFR estimating equations in a Finnish cohort of children and adolescents, which is distinc from the populations used in the development of the equations. Additionally, we assessed the accuracy of GFR estimation across different age groups and GFR categories.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Performance of GFR Estimation in Finnish Children and Adolescents》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patient Characteristics · p0090】The patient characteristics are presented in Table 1. The median age of the cohort was 9.1 (range: 0.8–19.9) years. Of the 516 patients, 273 patients (53%) were transplant recipients with 159 having received a kidney transplant, 61 a liver transplant, 40 a heart transplant, 2 a lung transplant, and 1 a small-bowel transplant and 10 patients having undergone multiorgan transplantation. Of note, 32 patients were diagnosed with a malignant neoplasm. One patient presented with glomerular hyperfiltration (mGFR > 135 ml/min per 1.73 m2). All laboratory values were sampled within 5 days of mGFR, with 356 patients (69%) having creatinine and cystatin C sampled on the day of GFR measurement. In the sensitivity analysis, the difference in sampling days did not have a significant effect (P = 0.06) on the relative error of CKiD U25 eGFRcr-cys (Supplementary Figure S1).

【Bias, Precision, and Accuracy of Selected eGFR Equations in the Entire Cohort · p0095】Median bias, IQR, and P10 and P30 accuracies for the selected eGFR equations for the entire cohort are presented in Table 2. CKiD (2012) eGFRcr-cys had the lowest median bias (0.1 [95% CI, −1.1 to 1.0] ml/min per 1.73 m2) and IQR (14.6 [95% CI, 13.2–16.3] ml/min per 1.73 m2) and the highest P10 and P30 accuracies (47.3% [95% CI, 43.0%–51.6%] and 94.6% [95% CI, 92.6%–96.5%], respectively) of all the equations. Other combination equations showed similar median bias (between 2.6 and 4.0 ml/min per 1.73 m2) and P30 accuracy, (between 86.4% and 90.1%) with overlapping CIs among themselves. The performance of selected combination equations is visualized in Figure 2.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Performance of GFR Estimation in Finnish Children and Adolescents》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】Our cohort consisted of 516 patients aged from 0.8 to 19.9 years with a history of solid organ transplantation, malignancy, or suspected kidney impairment. In general, creatinine-cystatin C-based combination equations exhibited better performance than single-analyte equations. Despite developed using cystatin C not calibrated to International Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (IFCC) reference material, the Chronic Kidney Disease in Children (CKiD) (2012) combination equation had the lowest median bias (0.1 ml/min per 1.73 m2), interquartile range (IQR; 14.6 ml/min per 1.73 m2), and the highest P10 and P30 accuracies (47.3% and 94.6%, respectively). Moreover, it surpassed the P30 threshold of 90% in all age groups. Other combination equations showed similar median bias (between 2.6 and 4.0 ml/min per 1.73 m2) and P30 accuracy (between 86.4% and 90.1%), with overlapping 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

【Conclusion · abstract-4-1】Combination equations provided more accurate estimates of GFR than single-analyte equations. Selected combination equations accurately estimated GFR across all age groups, a finding that is likely population dependent.

evidence.text: Our cohort consisted of 516 patients aged from 0.8 to 19.9 years with a history of solid organ transplantation, malignancy, or suspected kidney impairment. In general, creatinine-cystatin C-based combination equations exhibited better performance than single-analyte equations. Despite developed using cystatin C not calibrated to International Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (IFCC) reference material, the Chronic Kidney Disease in Children (CKiD) (2012) combination equation had the lowest median bias (0.1 ml/min per 1.73 m2), interquartile range (IQR; 14.6 ml/min per 1.73 m2), and the highest P10 and P30 accuracies (47.3% and 94.6%, respectively). Moreover, it surpassed the P30 threshold of 90% in all age groups. Other combination equations showed similar median bias (between 2.6 and 4.0 ml/min per 1.73 m2) and P30 accuracy (between 86.4% and 90.1%), with overlapping 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Combination equations provided more accurate estimates of GFR than single-analyte equations. Selected combination equations accurately estimated GFR across all age groups, a finding that is likely population dependent.

【Figure 1 · fig1】Figure 1 Flowchart of the data preparation procedure. The chart shows the inclusion criteria and the amount of excluded data in different steps of the process. From the remaining measurements the first measurement of each individual patient was selected, resulting in the final cohort (bold). BMI, body mass index; CysC, cystatin C; GFR, glomerular filtration rate; mGFR, measured GFR; SCr, serum creatinine.

【Figure 2 · fig2】Figure 2 Bland-Altman plots with local regression of selected combination eGFR equations in all patients. The values are presented in ml/min per 1.73 m2. The gray area represents the 95% confidence interval for the locally weighted scatterplot smoothing regression (solid line) calculated using bootstrapping (10,000 resamples). The dashed line represents the mean difference of eGFR equation and mGFR (eGFR − mGFR), and the dotted lines show the ±1.96 SD from the mean difference representing the 95% limits of agreement.
